records.publisher: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
records.shortExcerpt: This plant requires perfectly drained soil, preferably on the dry side, and full sun.
records.reviewerSummary: Species-scoped Tier A plant toolbox profile. Dry-side preference language is the water preference signal; drought-tolerant / dry-soil resistance attributes alone do not prove low. Overwatering causes root rot. Publication and update dates are not displayed. Do not reuse lavender-sun packets as water evidence.
records.normalizedClaim: Mature outdoor ground-grown Lavandula angustifolia prefers dry-side, well-drained culture and declines under persistently wet or overwatered conditions.

records.sourceTitle: Lavender: A must-have plant for all gardens
records.shortExcerpt: Newly planted lavender should be watered regularly the first year. Once established, lavender is drought-tolerant and should only be watered when the soil dries out.
records.reviewerSummary: English lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) centered. After-establishment water-when-soil-dries guidance supports low preferred water need; drought-tolerant label alone does not prove low. Establishment-year watering is outside the mature context. Container and raised-bed notes are planting-form caveats only. Displayed pull date 2020-05-02.
records.normalizedClaim: After establishment, mature outdoor ground-grown Lavandula angustifolia has a low preferred water need and should be watered only when the soil dries.
